This binding likely contributes to the observed relationship between Chlorthalidone and Ca12. The evidence is supported by a shared pathway involving thiazide diuretics and a common ancestor in the class of organonitrogen heterocyclic compounds. The strength of the relationship is indicated by the final score of 0.7175, suggesting a moderate to strong association. The mechanism involves the pharmacological interaction between the diuretic agents and their target protein, Ca12, through a shared biochemical pathway.
